intended_object: The standard functor from the category of cocones on a diagram F : J ⥤ C to the comma category (F ↓ Δ), where Δ = const J : C ⥤ (J ⥤ C) is the diagonal functor. It sends a cocone (X, ι : F ⟶ Δ X) to the arrow ι, and a cocone morphism to its underlying morphism. This comes from the docstring and the companion equivalence `Cocone.equivStructuredArrow`.
explanation: A cocone on F is exactly an object X together with a natural transformation F ⟶ (const J).obj X, so it is an object of `StructuredArrow F (const J)`. The definition sends c to `StructuredArrow.mk c.ι`. On morphisms it sends f to `StructuredArrow.homMk f.hom`. The commutativity this needs is precisely the cocone morphism condition `f.w`, which the automatic proof discharges. This is the textbook identification of cocones with the comma category (F ↓ Δ). It is the forward half of the equivalence `Cocone.equivStructuredArrow`. It is stated for arbitrary categories J and C with arbitrary universes, which is the natural generality. Since the file is itself part of Mathlib, there is no other Mathlib declaration of the same functor to cite.
